newsitem.title: portugal: RALLYING-MAKINEN LOOKING FOR CHANGE OF LUCK.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MAKINEN LOOKING FOR CHANGE OF LUCK.

text.p: Defending world rally drivers' champion Tommi Makinen and his Mitsubishi team head into this weekend's Portuguese rally confident they can kick-start their flagging season after a problem-riddled start.

Makinen, of Finland, is currently fifth in the drivers' championship with eight points, five behind leader Briton Colin McRae, after two third places and a non-finish in the opening rounds of this year's title race.
Mitsubishi are third behind Subaru and Ford in the manufacturers championship.
But both believe this could be the event where they enjoy a turn around in their fortunes and begin to reproduce the form which carried Makinen to glory last year.

"The car is very good, very reliable and the engine is very strong. We had a good test, so I think we can win Portugal," said Makinen, with unexpected confidence, despite having failed to finish the three Portuguese rallies he has started.

"Tommi is clearly a potential winner," said Mitsubishi team manager Phil Short. "We've led all three events so far through Tommi and had every chance of winning, so I hope we can convert this into a victory in Portugal.
"I think this rally will give a more accurate indication of the rest of the World Rally Championship than any of the first three rounds.
"Portugal is always one of the tougher rounds of the series. We're generally going quite long distances on rough roads, which are going to test car reliability and tyres."
The first of the 31 stages of the Rally of Portugal begins at the southern coastal resort of Figuiera da Foz on Sunday.
This is the first rally on the kind of loose gravel surfaces which the teams are likely to face in future rounds of the series.

"The first leg of the event is long and possibly the longest day in the world championship this year," McRae, who drives a Subaru Impreza, said. "It's going to be tough and important to establish a pace.
"The weather up there in the mountains is unpredictable as it's quite high and I would have thought that whoever leads out of there will be pretty much home and dry."
The event will finish on Wednesday in Figuiera after snaking east and south through the anticipated heavy showers expected during Portugal's wettest month of March.
